description: Current VotePredictor forecast for one 2026 US election: win probability, predicted margin, whether it comes from polls or fundamentals, how far it has moved this cycle, and the candidates. Accepts a state name or code ('Ohio', 'OH') or a district ('CA-12'). Returns an explicit refusal for races where a candidate has left the ballot and no forecast is published.

office.description: Which office: SEN for U.S. Senate, GOV for governor, HOUSE for a U.S. House district. Any case; 'senate' and 'governor' also work.

where.description: Where the race is: a state name ('Ohio'), a two-letter state code ('OH'), or a House district ('CA-12'). Pass what the user said.

name: forecast_race

actual_matchup.description: The contest actually on the ballot, when it is not Democrat vs Republican

as_of.description: Date of the model run behind this number

forecast_published.description: False when this site declines to publish a probability for the race

location.description: State code, or district id for the House

movement_points.description: BACKCAST change in win probability, in points, positive toward Democrats: today's model rerun on the polls available at each past date. Not how the published number moved; do not describe it as the forecast's history.

no_forecast_code.description: independent_contender: no Democrat is on the ballot and an independent challenges the Republican (nobody left the ballot; the model has no slot for an independent). nominee_changed: the polls on file ask about a former nominee. no_major_party_nominee: a side has nobody yet.

no_forecast_reason.description: Why nothing is published, in words. Do not substitute your own estimate.

p_basis.description: What set the win probability. 'shop_ratings': an unpolled House district whose probability blends in the rating shops' current ratings while pred_margin stays the lean model's, so the two can point different ways. Say so rather than treating it as an inconsistency.

p_dem_win.description: Democratic win probability, 0.01-0.99. Never 0 or 1: an election that has not happened is not certain.

rating.description: Safe D / Likely D / Lean D / Toss-up / Lean R / Likely R / Safe R

source.description: 'polls' where a poll-driven forecast exists, otherwise 'fundamentals' (lean, incumbency, national environment)

summary.description: One-paragraph answer suitable for reading aloud

title: Forecast a 2026 race
